# SharpMD

> SharpMD is a Markdown editor in the cloud where an AI and a team work on the same notes. It runs in the browser as a web app, a Chrome extension and an app on the phone, with an MCP endpoint, a REST API and webhooks already running: Claude, Codex or any other MCP client reads the notes before it works and writes down what it did. People edit on the formatted page, with no syntax to type, share by link and edit together live. The editor is free and open source, and a .md file or a folder from the disk opens without being uploaded. Folders with a password are encrypted in the browser, and the sync server can be self-hosted.

- Web app: https://sharpmd.app/src/app.html
- Site: https://sharpmd.app/ (Spanish: https://sharpmd.app/es/)
- Source code: https://github.com/MR-Axel/sharpmd (app under MIT, sync server under AGPL-3.0)
- Contact: hello@sharpmd.app

## What it does

- Edits Markdown in place: click a paragraph, a heading, a list item or a table cell and type. The Markdown source is rewritten block by block.
- Reads GitHub Flavored Markdown plus KaTeX math, Mermaid and Graphviz diagrams, footnotes, task lists, callouts, definition lists and YAML front matter.
- Opens a whole folder: file tree, search across every file, `[[name]]` links, create, rename, move and delete. Files and folders move by dragging, and a file dragged into the note being edited becomes a link.
- Block menu on right-click: insert a table, code block, diagram, formula or callout; turn into, move, duplicate, delete.
- Tables with totals and formulas (`=sum`, `=avg`, `=min`, `=max`, `=count`, `=median`), kanban boards from task lists, pasted images saved next to the document.
- Exports one standalone HTML file, or PDF through print.
- Read aloud (a tool turned on in Settings > Tools): reads the note, from a block or the selection, with the voices of the device. Code and diagrams are announced, not read.
- Dictation (a tool turned on in Settings > Tools): speech to text in English and Spanish with spoken commands for punctuation, headings, lists, tasks and formatting, a formula mode that produces LaTeX and a flowchart mode that produces Mermaid. It uses the speech recognition of the browser, on the device when available; SharpMD never receives audio.
- Presentation mode (a tool turned on in Settings > Tools): the open note as full screen slides, one per level 1 or 2 heading, with a divider as a manual split, keyboard and swipe navigation, an overview, a laser pointer, speaker notes written as `> [!NOTE]` quotes and PDF export through print.
- Daily note (a tool turned on in Settings > Tools): opens today's note or creates it from a template, as `YYYY-MM-DD.md` by default, in the browser, the cloud or a folder on disk. A month calendar marks the days that have a note. Works offline.
- Word export (a tool turned on in Settings > Tools): a .docx built in the browser without libraries, with Word heading styles, lists, task checkboxes, tables, code, footnotes, embedded images and diagrams as images. Formulas are exported as LaTeX text.
- Link map (a tool turned on in Settings > Tools): a graph of the links between notes (relative Markdown links and `[[wikilinks]]`) and a list of the notes that link to the open one. It reads only notes already on the device.
- AI assistant with your own key (a tool turned on in Settings > Tools, off by default): SharpMD provides no AI of its own. The person connects their own API key for Claude (Anthropic), OpenAI or an OpenAI-compatible server (OpenRouter, Ollama, LM Studio). It rewrites a selection or a block (improve, fix, shorten, expand, tone, translate, explain, free request) as a proposal with marked differences that is applied only on confirmation, generates Markdown in place (table, task list, Mermaid diagram, LaTeX formula, summary, key points, tasks), and answers questions about the open note in a side panel. Requests go from the browser straight to the chosen provider; the key is stored only on the device, encrypted with a non-exportable key, and SharpMD's server never receives the key or the text.
- Community gallery (Settings > Tools): templates, themes and diagram palettes shared by people and reviewed before they are published. Declarative content only, never code. What is added is stored on the device and works offline. Sharing needs an account; the public list (GET /gallery on the sync server) needs none.
- Twelve built-in themes (six light, six dark), picked from a grid of thumbnails with a live preview. Four are free; the other eight come with the paid plan. Each theme sets page, panels, text, borders, links, selection, code syntax and diagram colors, with AA contrast.
- On iPhone and iPad the web app installs from Safari (Share, Add to Home Screen). On a Mac the shortcuts use ⌘ and ⌥.
- Interface in English and Spanish.

## Where it runs

- Web app: nothing to install. Chrome, Edge and Brave open folders and save in place. Firefox and Safari open one file at a time and saving downloads a copy.
- Chrome extension: works without a connection and opens local .md files with a double-click once Chrome is the default app for them.
- Sync server: one Node file with SQLite. It can be self-hosted; the app takes its address in Settings.

## Cloud notes and AI

- Sign-in is a six-digit code sent by email, with no password.
- A note reaches the server only when the user sends it to the cloud. Files opened from disk are never uploaded.
- Sending a note to the cloud moves it there. A deleted cloud note stays in the trash for 30 days and can be restored; what is in the trash is not searched, shared or reachable over MCP.
- The account can be deleted from the app (Settings, Cloud, "Delete account"), which removes its notes and everything else stored for it.
- Cloud notes can be shared with another account, to read or to edit, or through a read-only public link with an optional password.
- Published sites: on the paid plan a cloud folder can be published as a public website (menu with the tree of pages, search, a theme), one site per account, when the server has a host for sites. Pages are rendered in the browser of whoever publishes and served from a separate host with a strict content policy. Protected folders are never published, and a note with `publish: false` in its front matter is left out. What an AI changes over MCP or the API stays unpublished until the person publishes it from the app. Each page links to a report form.
- Live sessions: the owner of a cloud note, on the paid plan, opens a session and hands out a link. Guests join from the browser with a name and no account, up to 12 people, and edit the same note at once. The secret of the link travels after the # of the address. On a team note, a member who can edit opens the session if the administrators allow it (they always can), and the other members who have the note open edit along from their account. A team space protected with a password has no live sessions.
- Who is here: a cloud note shows who has it open now and who edited it last. An AI that reads or writes a note with a token is shown there for a short while, with the name of the token and of the MCP client (`clientInfo.name` in `initialize`).
- MCP endpoint over Streamable HTTP at https://sync.sharpmd.app/mcp with seventeen tools: `list_notes`, `list_folders`, `read_note`, `write_note`, `append_note`, `search_notes`, `list_comments`, `resolve_comment`, `move_note`, `note_history`, `get_guide`, `list_boards`, `create_board`, `add_card`, `move_card`, `update_card`, `delete_card`. Authentication is a bearer token the user creates in the app, and a token can be limited to one folder.
- `write_note`, `append_note` and `move_note` return a link that opens the note in the web app.
- The board tools work on kanban boards inside a note: `create_board` makes one (by default To do, In progress, Paused, Done), `add_card`, `move_card`, `update_card` and `delete_card` change cards by id, and `list_boards` returns columns and cards. Each answer has the card id, its column and the link to the note. Moving a card to the done column marks it as done.
- `get_guide` returns the working guide for an AI agent: document the project in one folder (`README.md`, `architecture.md`, `features/`, `epics.md`, `decisions.md`, `log.md`) and keep a task board in `board.md`, one card per task, with the fields `agent`, `needs` and `link`. The message copied from Settings > AI (MCP) sets an agent up to do both without being asked.
- Five more tools exist only for a token the user created with the sharing permission, which is off by default: `list_shares`, `share_note`, `unshare_note`, `create_public_link`, `revoke_public_link`. They stay inside the folder of the token and do not reach protected folders. On team notes they work only when the administrators of the team allow members to share them.
- Settings > AI has a "Copy instructions for your AI" button: a message in English with how to connect and how to document work in SharpMD.
- Automations (paid plan), set up in Settings > Automations and documented at https://sharpmd.app/api.html: a REST API at https://sync.sharpmd.app/api/v1 with the same `mdt_` tokens as MCP (notes, folders, search, history, comments, and kanban boards as JSON with operations to create, move, update and complete a card); OpenAPI 3.1 at https://sync.sharpmd.app/api/v1/openapi.json; outgoing webhooks signed with HMAC-SHA-256 (`X-SharpMD-Signature`) for `note.created`, `note.updated`, `note.deleted`, `note.restored`, `note.moved`, `comment.created`, `comment.resolved`, `card.created`, `card.moved`, `card.updated`, `card.done`, `card.deleted`, scoped to the account, a folder or a note, with ready-made Slack and Discord formats; and inbound addresses (`POST /in/<secret>`) that append text to a note, create a note or create a card.
- A kanban card can end with attributes in braces: `- [ ] Fix checkout {due=2026-10-20 owner="Ana Paz" id=c8k2m9xq created=2026-10-07T14:03:11Z}`. `id`, `created` and `updated` are written by the app; the rest are free `key=value` pairs. A line `{show=due,owner priority=low|medium|high}` before the first column configures the board.
- Page settings live in the front matter of a note: `width: normal | wide | full`, `numbered: true` and `toc: false` (hides the outline of that note, also on its published page).
- The user can leave a comment on a passage of a note. The AI reads the open comments with `list_comments`, makes the change and closes each one with `resolve_comment`.
- Cloud notes are encrypted at rest on the server, which holds the key so it can share them and serve MCP.
- A folder can be protected with a password. Its notes are encrypted in the browser (AES-256-GCM, key wrapped with PBKDF2) and the server cannot read them. File and folder names stay visible. Protected folders are left out of sharing, public links and MCP, unless the user unlocks one for the AI for a set time; while unlocked, the server holds the key in memory only.
- On a team plan every member is an administrator, an editor or a reader. The token of a reader reads `@team/` notes and cannot change them. Administrators decide, for the team space, whether members share notes outside the team, create public links, open live sessions with guests, connect their AI or use automations, how long the version history is kept (up to a year) and the folder and template of new notes. They also create team tokens, which belong to the team and not to a person: with one, MCP sees the team space as the root, with plain paths and no `@team/` prefix, and it keeps working when its creator leaves. Administrators read an activity log of who did what in the space, with paths and never the text of the notes, kept for 90 days. Only the account that pays sees prices and billing.
- On a team plan the administrator can protect the whole team space with one password, in the same format. Members unlock it with that password, which they get from the administrator outside the app. Only the administrator changes the password, rotates the key or removes the protection. While the space is protected, `@team/` notes are closed to MCP unless the administrator unlocks them for their AI for a set time, or allows members to do the same for theirs. Server search, `move_note` and `note_history` do not work on a protected team space.

## Plans

- Free: the whole editor, unlimited files and browser notes, 10 notes in the cloud.
- Paid: USD 3.99 a month or USD 39 a year. Unlimited cloud notes, sharing and public links, live sessions, the MCP connection, automations (API, webhooks, inbound addresses), 30 days of version history, colors, fonts and custom CSS, and one published site (a folder of notes as a public website at pages.sharpmd.app).

## Privacy

- No analytics. Details: https://sharpmd.app/privacy.html
